output_exceptions: Initial broad manifest print was truncated; relied only on subsequent targeted, untruncated Calculator/Hate asset entries and directly verified image hashes.
One direct FAQ PDF page-4 text print was 6037 characters; re-read it in bounded contiguous ranges [0,6000) and [6000,6037). No text was truncated.
read_integrity.external_browsing_reason: The task is to determine what the supplied original and general FAQ actually establish. No additional publisher ruling was obtained; gaps are explicitly retained.

evidence.fact: A reinforcement is played on either side of the encounter after revelation and adds to that side’s total.
Explicitly permits any involved player to reinforce either side regardless of encounter cards, including attack/negotiate and negotiate/negotiate.
Answers No to whether one can play a reinforcement card on a negotiate.
A negotiate automatically loses against an attack; two negotiates cause an attempted deal.

adjudications.permissible_literal_reading: The p3 permission concerns playing a card on a side. Rulebook p13 assigns its bonus to that side’s total, rather than rewriting the encounter card’s type or printed value. Read narrowly, p4 could forbid treating a negotiate itself as a numerical attack card or adding a bonus directly to its value.
adjudications.inferred_reconciliation: The side-total versus encounter-card-value distinction makes the statements capable of coexisting. The sources never explicitly say that this is what p4 means, and the phrase on a negotiate could instead mean reinforcing its side. Calling this the official resolved interpretation would exceed the evidence.
adjudications.adjudication: Preserve both FAQ statements and flag their scope as unresolved. Do not silently replace the explicit p3 permission with a blanket ban, or claim a definite official reconciliation. Reinforcement alone does not state that a negotiate becomes an attack or that its normal negotiate outcome changes.
adjudications.would_resolve: Publisher clarification expressly explaining p4’s on a negotiate wording, or an edition-matched erratum withdrawing one of the two FAQ answers.

evidence.fact: The offense retrieves one ship to a colony; if there are no colonies, puts it directly in the hyperspace gate.
For a player with no colonies or ships on their turn, Regroup retrieves one ship from the warp and permits placement on any home planet.
Mobius Tubes with nowhere to return ships ordinarily returns them to the warp; offense may put up to four in the gate first. This is an effect-specific rule, not the Regroup answer.

adjudications.permissible_literal_reading: FAQ p4 gives a different destination for the particular recovery situation it names. Since the ship comes from the warp, no ships must mean no available ships in play, not literally owning zero physical ships anywhere.
adjudications.inferred_reconciliation: Treating later official FAQ clarification as modifying the earlier rule in its named case yields an operational rule: a wholly stranded offense with no colonies and no ships available in play may recover onto any home planet. This is an FAQ exception/clarification, not a conclusion derived from the original rule alone.
adjudications.adjudication: Report the FAQ’s named recovery case directly and attribute it. Do not state gate placement as an unconditional rule when the FAQ applies. The FAQ wording does not clearly settle whether its exception also covers every possible no-colony state with ships still in play, such as ships researching technology; retain the original gate rule outside the clearly described case unless a further ruling applies.
adjudications.remaining_scope_gap: No colonies or ships is idiomatic and not a formal condition specifying every off-planet ship location. A universal no-colonies-to-home-planet rule is broader than the clear shipless example.
adjudications.would_resolve: Publisher clarification specifying whether all no-colony situations use a home planet, or whether only a player with no ships in play receives that exception.

evidence.fact: Choose Aliens explicitly places the selected sheet facedown. Remaining setup steps do not direct a reveal.
Hidden Powers is a variant in which sheets are left facedown after selection and can be turned faceup at any time to enable use.
Losing and regaining powers uses facedown and faceup sheets, showing faceup is the ordinary active state.
No standard initial reveal-time instruction found.

adjudications.permissible_literal_reading: Standard setup initially places the sheet facedown. Hidden Powers expressly adds continued concealment. The book presupposes faceup, available powers in ordinary play, but omits the transition instruction.
adjudications.inferred_reconciliation: Revealing all chosen powers before ordinary play begins is a reasonable completion of the omission, supported by the contrast with the optional variant. Neither immediately after choosing nor a precise numbered setup step is expressly specified.
adjudications.adjudication: Record the missing standard reveal-time instruction. Do not label a chosen reveal step as verbatim original/FAQ law. Do not infer that the optional Hidden Powers procedure is the standard game simply because setup starts facedown.
adjudications.would_resolve: Edition-matched publisher erratum or explicit publisher answer stating when standard sheets are revealed.

evidence.fact: Declares equalize before reveal; if both are attacks, reduces the value of the higher card by the lower card. Example is 15 versus 8 becoming 7 versus 8. No equal-value clause is printed.
Morph copies the initially revealed value and can subsequently be modified separately. This does not adjudicate equal-value Calculator results.

adjudications.permissible_literal_reading: When both attacks have equal value, neither is higher than the other. The printed instruction therefore identifies no higher card to reduce; leaving both unchanged is a defensible literal application.
adjudications.inferred_reconciliation: Reducing both equal cards to zero, arbitrarily selecting one, or using offense/defense timing to break the equality requires an additional rule absent from the inspected sources. The timing rule orders players’ effects, not which equal attack counts as higher.
adjudications.adjudication: The source supports the literal no-higher-card/no-reduction reading, with the limitation that the equal case is not expressly stated. Do not present both-to-zero or one-to-zero as established. For an answer requiring a definitive intended equality rule, mark unresolved rather than upgrading this literal reading into explicit publisher confirmation.
adjudications.would_resolve: Publisher answer or original-edition erratum explicitly stating Calculator’s result on equal attack values, including an attack copied by Morph.

evidence.fact: If Hate discards an attack, opponents must discard an attack of equal or higher value to avoid losing ships.

Question asks whether an attack 04 may be discarded in response to Hate’s attack 20. Answer denies it and says without an attack higher than 20 one wishes to discard, discard nothing and lose three ships.

adjudications.permissible_literal_reading: The printed component expressly permits an equal attack. The FAQ’s higher than 20 sentence, taken as a general strict threshold, excludes that equal attack. Both agree that 04 cannot pay for 20.
adjudications.inferred_reconciliation: The FAQ may have omitted equal to while answering a question solely about a lower card. That contextual reading preserves the printed rule, but is an inference. Conversely, treating this as an intentional strict-higher erratum is also an inference: the FAQ does not label it as a change to Hate or ask about a second 20.
adjudications.adjudication: Record an unresolved equality-boundary discrepancy. It is safe to state the printed equal-or-higher rule with the FAQ caveat, and the definite shared conclusion that a lower attack cannot be discarded instead. It is not safe to assert either an intentional FAQ removal of equality or an officially confirmed FAQ typo.
adjudications.would_resolve: Publisher correction or answer explicitly addressing whether a second attack 20 may be discarded against Hate’s attack 20 in the original edition.
